exposure: Insulin injections without continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) sensor
outcome: Proportion of patients with diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA)
Proportion of patients with severe hypoglycemia (SH)
cohort: The study included 25,654 children and adolescents aged under 18 years, with type 1 diabetes of at least 1 year duration, who had documented pump or sensor usage during August 2017-July 2019, from the international SWEET registry.
finding: Participants using an insulin pump and/or continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) sensor had lower HbA1c and fewer DKA episodes compared to those using injections without a sensor, with pump use also associated with a lower rate of severe hypoglycemia and concomitant use of pump and CGM showing additive benefits.
